### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**39** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5272b1107a952e078764e0dfffb34539830e5bf1` — the merge of head `ec3a1429c9a87fc42a876ec60f2289d7ee5da233` into base `57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5272b1107a952e078764e0dfffb34539830e5bf1 && git checkout 5272b1107a952e078764e0dfffb34539830e5bf1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03 ec3a1429c9a87fc42a876ec60f2289d7ee5da233 && git checkout -B drift-repro 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03 && git merge --no-ff ec3a1429c9a87fc42a876ec60f2289d7ee5da233

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ec3a1429c9a87fc42a876ec60f2289d7ee5da233`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: accept-set narrowing at the in-process uninstall verb (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset; title `fix(metadata-protocol,runtime)!:`). No path under `packages/spec/**`, no ADR or skills file, no governed path, no new error code, no new route. Diff read in full: 11 files, +518/−13.
- **The seam is the before-half of the existing one.** `registerUninstallGuard(name, guard)` sits beside `registerUninstallCleanup` in the class-head facet, with the same Map-by-name shape and the same replace-on-re-register rule. `deletePackage` asks the guards in `askUninstallGuards` right after the retired-key refusal and before its first `sys_metadata` read. So a refusal moves nothing, pinned by five zero counts in `protocol.uninstall-guards.test.ts`. A guard's throw propagates, and the code fails closed on a guard that cannot judge. With no guard registered the loop is empty, and the bare-protocol CONTROL pins the old path.
- **Layering held.** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` imports nothing from the runtime and holds no copy of the rule. The verdict lives in the runtime and is registered once per protocol (WeakSet) from `AppPlugin.start`, beside `ensurePackageStateUninstallCleanup`. The registry is resolved when the guard is asked, not captured at boot.
- **One function for door and verb (rework 1).** `packageUninstallDependentRulesRefusal` builds `readDisableDependentRules` + `disableDependentRulesMessage(…, { operation: 'uninstall' })` as `409 PACKAGE_DISABLE_RESTRICTED_BY_VALIDATION_RULE`. Both the guard and the `DELETE /packages/:id` arm answer through it, so the two cannot drift. The door keeps its check ahead of `resolveProtocol` (seat ruling A): a host whose protocol has no `deletePackage` or no guard still gets the refusal, and #31227's "verb never reached" pin still holds. The dev's ablation shows the guard alone answers the identical 409, code and message.
- **The rollback callers.** The install-local pair-install undo (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` `pairInstallWriteFailure`) and the unmanaged-import rollback already catch a thrown uninstall and report it as residue. A refusal there leaves the partial package installed, says so, and logs at `error`. Nothing new is swallowed.

### ② Semver level

- Narrowing: an uninstall the verb performed for an in-process caller is now refused ⇒ BREAKING for those callers. It is declared with `!` and a **BREAKING** changeset paragraph covering Before, Now, the seam, Who moves and the remedy. The new method and the two exported types are additive. The `patch` bumps on both packages follow the repo's `changeset-no-major` practice for declared narrowings, as #31227 did.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security/permission boundary: none moved. The guard only reads the registry, and the door's `requireWritablePackage` and auth stay ahead of its check.
- Not closed here, filed: install-local's own `DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/:manifestId` withdraws through `registry.uninstallPackage` without the verb, so it asks neither guard nor audit → #31283.
- Merge needs the maintainer's per-PR word (narrowing).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-qrn7nl`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2dLQEXWGsE2SZ3Qn5F`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:server#4 · Head-sha: `ec3a1429c9a87fc42a876ec60f2289d7ee5da233`

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, `Fixes #31232` once, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial, `!` title, BREAKING changeset (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` + `@objectstack/runtime` patch). 11 files, +518/−13. Not governed, under 3000 lines. No spec, skills or ADR diff, so no Fable review is due.
- **Diff read by the seat:** guards are asked before the verb's first read, so a refusal moves nothing (five zero counts pinned). The runtime registers the doors' verdict once per protocol. The door and the guard share `packageUninstallDependentRulesRefusal` in its uninstall form, and the door keeps its check ahead of `resolveProtocol` (ruling A).
- **Premise measured:** with the guard call removed, the in-process `deletePackage` withdrew the field, and the next write answered `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (`qz_tier_known … No such key: qz_tier`). That is the break the card names (report round 0). The ablation turned 5 of 6 protocol pins and the in-process refusal pin red.
- **Gates (check-runs on the head):** 52 runs: 37 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed (`Test Core (8/8)` passed on its one re-run after the #31311 queue flake; audit 6715764127). Dev at ec3a1429c: `dispatch-gates --ran` 73/73, 0 NOT-MEASURED; runtime 8953 and metadata-protocol 22542 tests pass; typecheck and eslint exit 0 (report 6715746644).
- **Accepted deviations:** the dogfood battery was not rerun at ec3a1429c (declared narrowing: the rework delta is the door's call site and one builder argument, pinned by the runtime harness). It was last green in full at e052b1927, and CI's queue run carries the dogfood shards.
- **Out of scope:** install-local's own DELETE door bypasses the verb → #31283 (`finding`).
- **Landing:** Tier: none, but this is a BREAKING narrowing ⇒ it waits on the maintainer's word on this PR (`pm:awaiting-merge`). On approval: landing checks, label cleared, then `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.
